title: Impact of Unemployment Benefit Eligibility on Future Earnings

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
This calls for a Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) since we have a sharp cutoff at age for unemployment benefit eligibility. The key assumption is that individuals just below and just above the age cutoff are similar in all unobservable characteristics except for treatment status. We expect a discontinuous jump in future earnings at the cutoff if unemployment benefits have a causal effect.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(rdrobust)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s87_data.csv")

# Check data structure
head(data)
summary(data)

# Center running variable around cutoff (appears to be at 0)
# Based on the preview, cutoff seems to be around 0.5 or between treated/control
cutoff <- 0.5  # This appears to be the cutoff based on the data pattern

# Create centered running variable
data$age_centered <- data$running_var - cutoff

# Main RDD analysis using rdrobust
rdd_result <- rdrobust(y = data$y, 
                      x = data$running_var, 
                      c = cutoff,
                      p = 1,  # linear specification
                      kernel = "triangular")

# Print main results
cat("=== MAIN RDD RESULTS ===\n")
cat("Treatment Effect (RDD Coefficient):", round(rdd_result$coef[1], 4), "\n")
cat("Standard Error:", round(rdd_result$se[1], 4), "\n")
cat("95% Confidence Interval: [", round(rdd_result$ci[1,1], 4), ",", round(rdd_result$ci[1,2], 4), "]\n")
cat("P-value:", round(rdd_result$pv[1], 4), "\n")
cat("Bandwidth:", round(rdd_result$bws[1,1], 4), "\n")
cat("Number of observations:", rdd_result$N[1] + rdd_result$N[2], "\n")

# Robustness checks
cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECKS ===\n")

# 1. Different bandwidth
rdd_robust_bw <- rdrobust(y = data$y, 
                         x = data$running_var, 
                         c = cutoff,
                         h = rdd_result$bws[1,1] * 1.5)
cat("1. Larger bandwidth (1.5x optimal):", round(rdd_robust_bw$coef[1], 4), 
    "(SE:", round(rdd_robust_bw$se[1], 4), ")\n")

# 2. Quadratic specification
rdd_quad <- rdrobust(y = data$y, 
                    x = data$running_var, 
                    c = cutoff,
                    p = 2)
cat("2. Quadratic specification:", round(rdd_quad$coef[1], 4), 
    "(SE:", round(rdd_quad$se[1], 4), ")\n")

# 3. Uniform kernel
rdd_uniform <- rdrobust(y = data$y, 
                       x = data$running_var, 
                       c = cutoff,
                       kernel = "uniform")
cat("3. Uniform kernel:", round(rdd_uniform$coef[1], 4), 
    "(SE:", round(rdd_uniform$se[1], 4), ")\n")

# 4. Manual regression around cutoff for comparison
bandwidth <- rdd_result$bws[1,1]
local_data <- data[abs(data$running_var - cutoff) <= bandwidth, ]

manual_reg <- lm(y ~ I(running_var >= cutoff) + I(running_var - cutoff), 
                data = local_data)
cat("4. Manual linear regression:", round(coef(manual_reg)[2], 4), 
    "(SE:", round(summary(manual_reg)$coefficients[2,2], 4), ")\n")

# Summary statistics by treatment status
cat("\n=== DESCRIPTIVE STATISTICS ===\n")
treated_mean <- mean(data$y[data$treated == 1])
control_mean <- mean(data$y[data$treated == 0])
cat("Mean earnings (treated):", round(treated_mean, 4), "\n")
cat("Mean earnings (control):", round(control_mean, 4), "\n")
cat("Raw difference:", round(treated_mean - control_mean, 4), "\n")

# Plot the RDD
rdplot(y = data$y, 
       x = data$running_var, 
       c = cutoff,
       title = "RDD: Unemployment Benefit Eligibility on Future Earnings",
       x.label = "Age (Running Variable)", 
       y.label = "Log Earnings (2 years later)")

cat("\n=== FINAL ESTIMATE ===\n")
cat("The causal effect of unemployment benefit eligibility on future earnings is:")
cat(round(rdd_result$coef[1], 4), "log points")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive coefficient of approximately 0.10-0.25 log points. This would indicate that becoming eligible for unemployment benefits increases future earnings by roughly 10-25%. The mechanism could be that unemployment benefits allow individuals to search longer for better job matches rather than accepting the first available position, leading to higher-quality employment and better future earnings. Alternatively, benefits might provide stability that allows for skill development or retraining during unemployment spells.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: The cutoff age for benefit eligibility provides a natural experiment to assess causal impacts.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Eligibility for unemployment benefits at the cutoff age increases log earnings two years later.
